history.summary: The Sri Ayyappa Temple in Sector 5, Bokaro Steel City was established on 11 July 1983 and is managed by the Ayyappa Seva Sangham Bokaro Steel City, which runs an administrative office for the shrine. Besides Lord Ayyappa in the sanctum, the temple houses shrines for Ganesha, Kartikeya, Bhagavati, and Ram-Sita, serving the South Indian and broader Malayali/Kerala-origin devotee community of the steel city. The temple maintains an official website (ayyappatemplebokaro.in). The festival calendar was not documented in the sources consulted (flag: verify festival dates and the 1983 founding date with the Ayyappa Seva Sangham).

name: Ayyappa Temple
town_description: Bokaro Steel City is a planned industrial city in Bokaro district, Jharkhand, built around the Bokaro Steel Plant, one of India's major steel plants. Its numbered sectors host a large migrant workforce and community from across India.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi (nearest major airport)
travel.road: Sector 5, Bokaro Steel City, Jharkhand 827009; reachable by city roads

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Mandala/Makaravilakku season (November-January) is spiritually significant for Ayyappa devotees — verify festival calendar locally
visitor_information.opening_hours: Justdial lists morning hours 5:30 AM to 9:30 AM with the temple open until 8:30 PM; evening hours not consistently documented — verify locally
